subject: Economics
description: Covers GDP, GNP, NNP, expenditure method, GDP deflator, and disposable income.

questions.stem: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is best defined as:

options.option_text: The total market value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country in a given period
The total income earned by the citizens of a country, regardless of where they reside in the world
The sum of all intermediate and final goods produced by a countrys citizens in a year
The total value of goods and services produced minus the value of depreciation of capital assets

questions.explanation: GDP DEFINITION: Key elements are: (1) MARKET VALUE (monetary measure). (2) FINAL goods and services (intermediate goods are excluded to avoid double counting). (3) WITHIN DOMESTIC TERRITORY (geographical boundary, regardless of whether produced by citizens or foreigners). (4) GIVEN PERIOD (usually a year or quarter). GNP (Gross National Product) measures production by CITIZENS, regardless of location (GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad). NDP (Net Domestic Product) is GDP minus depreciation. PYQ FREQUENCY: Basic macroeconomics, tested in all exams.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: How is Net National Product at Factor Cost (NNPfc), which is officially considered as the "National Income", calculated from GDP at Market Price?

options.option_text: GDP at Market Price + Net Factor Income from Abroad - Depreciation - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies
GDP at Market Price - Depreciation - Net Factor Income from Abroad + Indirect Taxes
GDP at Market Price + Depreciation + Indirect Taxes - Subsidies
GDP at Market Price + Net Factor Income from Abroad + Depreciation

questions.explanation:
STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
1. From Domestic to National: GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA) = GNP (Gross National Product).
2. From Gross to Net: GNP - Depreciation = NNP (Net National Product at Market Price).
3. From Market Price to Factor Cost: Market Price includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies. Factor Cost is the actual cost of production. So, NNP at Market Price - Indirect Taxes + Subsidies = NNP at Factor Cost (NNPfc).
NNPfc is the standard measure of National Income. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-3, SSC CGL Tier 2.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: When calculating GDP using the expenditure method, which of the following formulas is used?

options.option_text: GDP = Consumption (C) + Investment (I) + Government Spending (G) + Net Exports (X - M)
GDP = Rent + Wages + Interest + Profit
GDP = Total Value of Output - Value of Intermediate Consumption
GDP = Private Consumption + Government Spending + Depreciation

questions.explanation: EXPENDITURE METHOD: Calculates GDP by summing all expenditures on final goods and services. Formula: C + I + G + (X - M). Where C = Private Final Consumption Expenditure, I = Gross Domestic Capital Formation (Investment), G = Government Final Consumption Expenditure, and (X - M) = Exports minus Imports (Net Exports). RENT + WAGES + INTEREST + PROFIT is the INCOME METHOD formula. OUTPUT - INTERMEDIATE CONSUMPTION is the VALUE ADDED (Production) METHOD. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, CDS, NDA.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions is INCLUDED in the calculation of a countrys GDP?

options.option_text: The commission earned by a real estate broker for selling a second-hand house
The sale value of a second-hand car sold directly between two individuals
Transfer payments such as old-age pensions given by the government
The value of unpaid domestic work performed by a homemaker

questions.explanation:
GDP INCLUSIONS/EXCLUSIONS: GDP measures CURRENT production. 
- EXCLUDED: Second-hand goods (already counted in the year they were produced), Financial transactions (shares, bonds), Transfer payments (pensions, scholarships — no productive service rendered), Unpaid domestic work (hard to value/non-market).
- INCLUDED: Brokerage/commission on second-hand sales (the broker provided a NEW service this year), imputed rent of owner-occupied houses, production for self-consumption (e.g., farmers consuming their own grain). PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC GS-3, CA Foundation.
questions.subject: Economics

options.option_text: The ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP, used as a broad measure of inflation in the economy
The depreciation of capital assets over the financial year
The difference between Gross Domestic Product and Net Domestic Product
The percentage of GDP lost due to underground economy and tax evasion

questions.explanation: GDP DEFLATOR: An index of price changes of goods and services included in GDP. Formula: (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100. NOMINAL GDP is measured at current prices. REAL GDP is measured at constant (base year) prices. The GDP deflator is the most comprehensive measure of inflation because it covers ALL domestically produced goods and services (including capital goods and government services), unlike the CPI or WPI which are based on a limited basket of goods. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, RBI Grade B.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Personal Disposable Income (PDI) represents the amount of money households actually have available for spending and saving. It is calculated as:

options.option_text: Personal Income minus Direct Personal Taxes and non-tax payments (like fines)
National Income minus Corporate Taxes and Retained Earnings
Gross Domestic Product minus Depreciation and Indirect Taxes
Personal Income minus Indirect Taxes and Subsidies

questions.explanation:
PERSONAL DISPOSABLE INCOME (PDI): The actual income households can spend or save. Calculation:
1. National Income (NNPfc)
2. minus Undistributed corporate profits, corporate taxes, net interest payments by households
3. plus Transfer payments to households (pensions, welfare)
= PERSONAL INCOME (PI).
4. PI minus Direct Personal Taxes (Income Tax) and non-tax payments (fines, fees)
= PERSONAL DISPOSABLE INCOME. PDI = Consumption + Savings. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, Bank PO.

questions.stem: In India, the base year currently used for calculating Real GDP and National Income is:
questions.explanation: BASE YEAR REVISION: In 2015, the Central Statistics Office (CSO, now NSO) revised the base year for National Accounts from 2004-05 to 2011-12. This revision also aligned India's GDP calculation with the UN System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008, shifting the headline growth measure from GDP at Factor Cost to GDP at constant Market Prices. Further revisions to base year (e.g., to 2022-23) are under discussion but 2011-12 remains the current official base year. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB NTPC, State PSCs.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Transfer payments are excluded from a country's National Income calculations because they:

options.option_text: Are received only by non-resident foreign nationals
Do not correspond to any current productive activity or output
Are already subject to income tax and hence double-counted
Are recorded separately under government capital expenditure

questions.explanation: B is correct because transfer payments (pensions, scholarships, unemployment benefits) involve no exchange of goods or services — they are mere income redistributions and hence excluded from National Income. Option A is wrong because transfer payments also go to domestic residents; option C is wrong because National Income measurement is independent of whether income is taxed.

questions.stem: Which of the following equations correctly relates two National Income aggregates?

options.option_text: NNP at Market Price = GDP at Market Price minus Depreciation
NDP at Market Price = GDP at Market Price minus Depreciation
GDP at Factor Cost = GDP at Market Price plus Net Indirect Taxes
NNP at Factor Cost = GDP at Market Price minus Net Indirect Taxes

questions.explanation: B is correct: NDP at MP = GDP at MP minus Consumption of Fixed Capital (Depreciation). Option A is wrong because subtracting depreciation from GDP gives NDP, not NNP — to get NNP you must first add NFIA to obtain GNP. Option C is wrong because GDP at FC = GDP at MP minus (not plus) Net Indirect Taxes. Option D wrongly starts from GDP instead of GNP.

questions.stem: Which of the following income items is included in India's National Income (NNP at FC) but NOT in India's Domestic Income (NDP at FC)?

options.option_text: Wages of Indian workers employed in Mumbai's textile mills
Profits of a South Korean electronics firm's factory in Pune
Salary of an Indian diplomat posted at the Indian Embassy in Tokyo
Income of a foreign tourist spending on hotels and travel in Kerala

questions.explanation: C is correct because National Income = Domestic Income + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). An Indian diplomat in Tokyo earns income outside India's domestic territory but remains an Indian resident, so it enters NFIA and is included in NI but not in Domestic Income. Option B (South Korean firm's profit in Pune) is included in Domestic Income but flows out as factor income abroad, so it is excluded from National Income.

questions.stem: In the Value Added Method of computing National Income, which of the following is NOT classified as 'intermediate consumption' and should therefore NOT be deducted while computing a firm's Gross Value Added?

options.option_text: Steel sheets purchased by a car manufacturer to fabricate vehicle bodies
Electricity consumed by a garment factory during the production process
A new CNC machine bought by a firm expected to last for the next 6 years
Packaging material purchased by a food processing plant for its products

questions.explanation: C is correct because a CNC machine lasting 6 years is a capital/durable good (recorded as Gross Fixed Capital Formation), not an intermediate good. Intermediate consumption covers only items fully used up within the current accounting period. Options A, B, and D are all consumed within the production period and are correctly classified as intermediate consumption, deducted while computing GVA.

questions.stem: A nation's 'Green GDP' differs from its conventional GDP primarily because Green GDP additionally:

options.option_text: Excludes income of non-resident foreign workers employed domestically
Deducts costs of environmental damage and depletion of natural resources
Counts only output from renewable energy and certified green industries
Adds imputed value of unpaid domestic work such as cooking and childcare

questions.explanation: B is correct: Green GDP = Conventional GDP minus monetised cost of environmental degradation minus value of depleted natural resources. It adjusts GDP downward to reflect ecological costs of growth. Option A describes the GDP-to-GNP transition (NFIA adjustment). Option D relates to satellite national accounts that capture non-market household production — a separate concept entirely from Green GDP.

questions.stem: An economy reports: GDP at Market Price = ₹180 lakh crore; Indirect Taxes = ₹24 lakh crore; Subsidies = ₹6 lakh crore; Depreciation = ₹14 lakh crore; Net Factor Income from Abroad = −₹2 lakh crore. What is the NNP at Factor Cost?

options.option_text: ₹140 lakh crore (National Income)
₹146 lakh crore (National Income)
₹148 lakh crore (National Income)
₹150 lakh crore (National Income)

questions.explanation: NNP at FC = GDP at MP + NFIA − Depreciation − Net Indirect Taxes. Net Indirect Taxes = 24 − 6 = ₹18 lakh crore. So: 180 + (−2) − 14 − 18 = ₹146 lakh crore. Option C (₹148) results from ignoring NFIA entirely. Option D (₹150) results from wrongly adding NFIA (+2) instead of subtracting (−2). Option A (₹140) results from using gross indirect taxes (₹24) instead of net indirect taxes (₹18), omitting the subsidies adjustment.

questions.stem: As per India's National Accounts Statistics (base year 2011-12), which identity correctly expresses the link between GDP at Market Prices and Gross Value Added (GVA) at Basic Prices?

options.option_text: GDP at MP = GVA at Basic Prices + Taxes on products − Subsidies on products
GDP at MP = GVA at Basic Prices − Taxes on production + Subsidies on production
GDP at MP = GVA at Basic Prices + All indirect taxes − All government subsidies
GDP at MP = GVA at Basic Prices + Taxes on products + Other taxes on production

questions.explanation: A is correct: GDP at MP = GVA at Basic Prices + Net taxes on products (Taxes on products minus Subsidies on products). GVA at basic prices already embeds 'other taxes on production' (e.g., property tax, professional tax levied on firms) and excludes only product-specific taxes (GST, excise, import duties). Option C is wrong because 'all indirect taxes' would double-count other production taxes already inside GVA. Option D wrongly re-adds both product taxes and other production taxes on top of a GVA that has already absorbed the latter.
